findings.title: Ledger post failure silently swallowed before gateway refund fires
findings.proof: refund.py:31-34 catches bare Exception from ledger.post and passes silently — no log, no re-raise, no cause preserved. Execution then proceeds unconditionally to gateway.refund at line 37, which moves money via the live v2 API (gateway.py) regardless of ledger write success. This means a ledger write failure produces no audit record and no operator visibility while the refund is still issued, a genuine financial-integrity error-masking bug.

findings.title: Self-admitted duplicate-refund risk left unaddressed
findings.proof: FIXME at refund.py:35 names duplicate-refund risk from gateway-side retries. The only dedup guard is `_seen` (refund.py:14,27-29), an in-memory, per-process set keyed on order_id at the start of issue() -- it does not gate the actual gateway.refund() call from being retried by the gateway itself, and resets on process restart. No ticket reference found in code or tests. The named risk is genuinely still present: nothing in gateway.py (idempotency key, dedup header) mitigates it either. Severity 5 (money duplication) and effort M (needs idempotency key design, not a one-liner) both look right.

findings.title: Entry sign-flip construction duplicated in refund.py and ledger.py

evidence.quote: entry = Entry(account=refund.order_id, amount_cents=-refund.amount_cents, reason=refund.reason_code)

def reverse(entry: Entry) -> Entry:
    return Entry(account=entry.account, amount_cents=-entry.amount_cents, reason="reversal")

findings.proof: The 'duplication' is a single-expression pattern — negating amount_cents inside an Entry(...) construction — appearing once in refund.py:30 (building a fresh refund entry) and once in ledger.py:29-30 (reverse(), building a reversal entry from an existing one). These serve different domains (initial posting vs. explicit reversal) and are too trivial (one field negation) to warrant a shared abstraction; extracting it would add indirection for no real maintenance benefit.
